trendsPage.lead: Split into three charts by venue category — years on the x-axis, accepted-paper counts on the y-axis. A line breaks for any year a venue didn't run, rather than dropping to 0.
trendsPage.needsJs: These charts need JavaScript to display. Please enable it and reload this page.

timelinePage.lead: Full submission cycles for the four major security venues. Dates are transcribed by hand from official sites and may change — always confirm with the official CFP.

home.metaDescription: Search papers, acceptance trends, abstracts, awards and submission deadlines across 10 top venues including IEEE S&P, USENIX Security, ACM CCS and NDSS.
home.headline:
Ten top venues,
one place to read them
home.lead: IEEE S&P, USENIX Security, ACM CCS and NDSS, plus ICSE / ISSTA / FSE / ASE / ASPLOS / SOSP. Accepted lists, abstracts, awards and submission deadlines — all in one site.
home.matrixLead: Darker means more papers accepted that year. Blank means the venue did not run, or is not yet indexed.
home.matrixNote: {total} papers total · each group normalized separately (Big Four peak {topMax}, SE / Systems peak {seMax})
home.f1Title:
One query,
fifteen thousand papers deep
home.f1Body: Full title matching, stackable venue and year filters, matches highlighted in place. Starred favorites stay in your own browser — nothing is uploaded.
home.f2Title:
A decade of growth,
in one line
home.f2Body: Acceptance counts by venue, by year, by group. All venues together went from {from} papers in 2015 to {to} in 2025 — whether that means easier or harder is for you to read off the chart.
home.f3Title:
Read the abstract
before opening IEEE
home.f3Body: Browse by venue and year with abstracts expanded inline. Your saved keywords get marked up automatically, so one glance tells you whether it is worth the click.
home.f4Title:
The next deadline,
and days remaining
home.f4Body: Full cycles for the Big Four: abstract registration, paper submission, rebuttal, notification, camera-ready. Countdowns computed in your local timezone.
home.f5Title:
Who took
Best Paper this year
home.f5Body: Best paper, outstanding paper and distinguished paper awards across the Big Four, grouped by year and by award. A quick read on where the field is heading.
home.f5MoreDetail: Every award, every year, Big Four
home.closingTitle: A few things built along the way
home.closingSitesBody: Curated external resources: venue rankings, CCF tiers, review process notes.
home.closingPrefsBody: Theme, accent color, watched keywords and favorites — all stored locally in your browser.
home.closingOpenBody: The Python code that crawls, parses and LLM-classifies the data is on GitHub.

moreSites.title: More Sites
moreSites.subtitle: A curated list of useful resources for academic security research and conference tracking. Click any card to open in a new tab.

bestPaperAwards.title: Best Paper Awards in Computer Science
bestPaperAwards.desc: A long-running collection of best paper awards across 32 computer science conferences since 1996, maintained by Jeff Huang.

ccfddl.title: CCF Conference Deadlines
ccfddl.desc: Tracks upcoming submission deadlines for conferences listed in the CCF recommended catalog, organized by topic and tier.

ccfRecommend.title: CCF Recommended Conferences and Journals
ccfRecommend.desc: An accessible mirror of the China Computer Federation's recommended catalog of international conferences and journals (Tier A/B/C).

connectedPapers.title: Connected Papers
connectedPapers.desc: Visualize related work as an interactive graph: enter a seed paper and explore prior work, derivative work, and similar papers in your field.

wisPaper.title: WisPaper
wisPaper.desc: AI-powered literature search that takes natural-language queries and uses Intent Verification to surface the papers most relevant to your research goal.

csPapers.title: CS Papers
csPapers.desc: A search engine for computer science conference papers (csrankings.org venues, including the security top tier) with fast filtering by venue/year and an open API.
